conclusion: The graph/Ramsey arm is provably a dead end at the level it was briefed: k=2 residue graphs with gcd(A)=1 can cover K_n for every n, so no cover, Ramsey, rank or container theorem can bound |A| from the incidence data alone. What the arm does yield is one conditional sharpening (elements coprime to prod S give |A| <= 2^k, better than 3*2^(k-1)) and, once the exact valuations are used rather than the graph, a rigorous one-directional reduction g(k) <= 3 + N_3(k) to counting nondegenerate solutions of x+y+z=1 in S-units over the same k primes.
confidence: High on the four theorems: each is a short proof written out in RESULTS.md, and each is confirmed on the parent's own seven witnesses by a stdlib probe that reruns in three seconds. High on the refutation of the parent's '|A| <= p-1 when p not in S' thread, which has an explicit verified witness {1,4,124} with S={2,5}. Medium on the framing of Theorem 4 as a live door: the two literature bounds cited (Evertse's exponential upper bound, the Erdos-Stewart-Tijdeman exp((4+o(1))(s/log s)^{1/2}) lower bound) were checked by web search rather than read in the sources, and no search was run for whether the reduction itself is folklore. Assume it is folklore until searched.

notes_for_operator: The parent asked for a sharper cover theorem or a realizable obstruction. It gets both, and they are the same finding seen from two sides: the cover structure is so rigid that it is nearly information-free, so the sharpening only exists under an arithmetic hypothesis. The one thing worth carrying forward past this arm is Theorem 4, because it converts Erdos #126 into a statement about S-unit equation counting whose known lower bounds are exp(k^{1/2+o(1)}), that is, consistent with the conjecture, so the door is open rather than closed. That is a different verdict from r_186989's door list, which named the S-unit machinery as the wall; it is more precisely the same open gap as the conjecture, not an obstruction to it. Note also that r_186989's door 1 (optimise S per k) is under the ceiling my Theorem 3 sets, so funding it buys constants at best.
